title: Workflows & orchestration
summary: Use explicit stages and acceptance criteria, with models performing analysis inside the process.

sections.label: Recommended architecture
sections.text: Start with one bounded outcome. Identify the steps, their inputs and outputs, who performs them and what happens after each check. Share useful instructions and controls where their assumptions fit.

sections.label: Control and judgment
sections.text: For an automated process, code enforces state transitions, permissions and limits. Models can investigate ambiguity, propose results and explain findings. A manual process can use the same explicit steps and checks with people responsible for them.

sections.label: Platform choice
sections.text: Check whether existing automation and CI can meet the need. Atlassian Automation and Jenkins are examples. Evaluate durable execution when restart recovery, long waits or reliable resumption of external actions justify it.

sections.label: Apply proportionately
sections.text: Distinguish the work of developing a capability from what the finished application does for each request. A study may end in a decision package. It does not require building an execution platform.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Choose proportionate orchestration from actual task dependencies and recovery requirements.
Record each step's input, output, actor and failure destination.
Compare existing automation with any proposed durable runner using observed requirements.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

catalog.applicability: Use this explanation to inform decisions. Confirm its fit with your actual environment.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
